summary: Attacked the library audit AUDIT-23, which covers five roadmaps (ProfiniteCohomology, StablePeriodicCurved, AutomorphicCongruences, AutomorphicPadicLFunctions, ColemanIntegration) in 45 layer entries with 304 targets and 696 declaration citations. The audit holds up: every citation resolves at the pinned commits in its cited file and line, none is private or sorried, no target's library field contradicts its citations, no layer verdict contradicts its targets, the statements read at the pin provide what their targets claim, the partial verdicts are right where they say a degree range is incomplete, and no target marked absent is in the libraries under another name. One finding, of low severity: the five roadmaps have 46 stages and the audit has 45 entries; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein is covered by no entry here and by no other audit, so its coverage is unrecorded.
checked: Every one of the 696 declaration citations across all 304 targets, against the declarations index at the pinned commits (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474): all exist, each in the file it is cited from and within twelve lines of the line it is cited at, and no target's citation is tagged with the wrong library. The single apparent exception, ModularForm.L cited at Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean line 134, is correct: the declaration is there, inside `namespace ModularForm`, and the index drops the namespace for several declarations in that file. REV-AUDIT-23 records the same observation, independently.

Whether any cited declaration is unusable: none of the 696 is private, and none of the 272 distinct cited files contains a `sorry` anywhere in the body of a cited declaration. All 272 files were opened.

Internal consistency of the result file: no target whose library field is mathlib, tauceti or both cites declarations from a different library; no layer with verdict 'not built' contains a target marked built; no target marked absent carries an exact-fit citation.

The discrete-versus-continuous surface, which is the distinction the ProfiniteCohomology roadmap turns on: every exact-fit Mathlib citation standing behind a target whose text mentions continuity, profiniteness, open or closed subgroups, or all degrees. All are right, including the hypotheses the notes name: Pi.discreteTopology needs [Finite iota] and the note says so; ContinuousMap.uncurry and Homeomorph.curry need local compactness, which profinite G satisfies, and the note says so; TopRep is a definition with an equivalence to Action (TopModuleCat R) G rather than an abbreviation for it, and the note says so.

Statements read at the pin, chosen where a target makes a claim that could fail: explicitCor0_comp_res0, explicitCor1_comp_res1 and explicitCor2_comp_res2 all exist and all read `= U.index • x`, so cor composed with res is multiplication by the index in each of the three degrees the target claims; oneObjectHomologicalComplex takes an object with an endomorphism d and a proof d comp d = 0, which is the differential module of its target; LinearMap.IsFrobeniusFunctional.moduleInjective_self gives Module.Injective A A and moduleInjective_op_self gives Module.Injective Aᵐᵒᵖ A, the left and right self-injectivity the target claims; TauCeti.WreathProduct is (iota -> D) semidirect Equiv.Perm iota with PermSubgroupWreathProduct for Q a subgroup, as its target describes.

The two partial verdicts that rest on a degree range being incomplete: the audit says Shapiro's lemma and the finite-quotient colimit theorem exist in degrees 0 and 1 but not 2. The index has explicitShapiro0, explicitShapiro1 and their apply and symm_apply lemmas with bijective_explicitShapiroMap1, and explicitFiniteQuotientColimit0 and explicitFiniteQuotientColimit1, and nothing in degree 2 in either family. Both partial verdicts are right.

The audit's sharpest technical claim, that Tau Ceti's logOneAdd specializes to p-adic fields as a definition but that its convergence is proved only under [ContinuousSMul NNRat K], which p-adic fields fail. Verified at TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Algebra/LogOneAdd/Basic.lean: the variable block at line 81 carries [CharZero K] [ContinuousSMul NNRat K] and governs one_le_logOneAddSeries_radius at line 84 and summable_logOneAdd at line 107, while the definition of logOneAdd at line 66 sits under a weaker block and does not need it. The note is exactly right.

The 184 targets marked absent, for mathematics the libraries have under another name, by concept search over the declarations index and then the source trees. Bockstein operators, the Evens norm, cohomological dimension of profinite groups, Gorenstein-projective modules, matrix factorizations, Happel's theorem, Positselski's derived categories of the second kind, p-adic polylogarithms, complete resolutions and stable module categories have no declaration at the pin. The one case where a library statement does exist is Hilbert 90, and the audit already cites it: groupCohomology.H1ofAutOnUnitsUnique is recorded as a special case, the missing statement is correctly identified as the profinite one, and the note adds that Mathlib's own Hilbert90.lean lists the infinite case as a TODO.

Duplication, both what the audit records and what it might have missed. The 39 recorded entries name a specific other layer and say what it owns. StablePeriodicCurved is the one roadmap with no recorded duplicates at all, across nine layers, so its mathematics was searched for in every other roadmap's stages: matrix factorizations, singularity categories, Frobenius exact categories, totally acyclic complexes, maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules, curved DG algebras, orbit categories, Verdier quotients, and the names Buchweitz, Orlov, Eisenbud and Happel occur in no other roadmap. The three near hits were read and are different mathematics: DGAInfinity layer 11 states the derived/coderived equivalence only as part of Koszul duality for augmented DG algebras, EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5 builds stable infinity-categories, and RefinedTraceMethods RT.5 builds localizing motives. Zero recorded duplicates is the right answer, not an omission.

Completeness of each audited layer against the text of its stage: for all 45 entries, the audit's targets against the milestones of the stage description. Only StablePeriodicCurved layer 8 has materially fewer targets than milestones, three against eight, and that is a deliberate collapse rather than an omission: its first target names all eight comparison functors together and its note says which one exists, in what weaker form, and that the other seven are absent.
Coverage of the five roadmaps' stages by the audit's layer entries. This produced the finding below: 45 entries against 46 stages.

findings.claim: The audit covers 45 of the 46 stages of the five roadmaps it audits. The AutomorphicPadicLFunctions roadmap has nine stages and the audit has eight entries for it; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein has none. No other audit covers it either, and it does not appear in the integrated data/library-coverage.json, so the library coverage of that stage is unrecorded. A worker sent to plan it, who is told to read the reviewed library audit before planning anything, finds nothing for it.
findings.evidence: The roadmap extract research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_AutomorphicPadicLFunctions.json (read at the repository head) lists nine stages: L0, L1, L2, L3, L3h, L4, L4e, L5 and KU-hilberteisenstein. The audit's layers dictionary for that roadmap has the first eight and not the ninth. Grepping research/blueprint/audit/ for KU-hilberteisenstein returns no file, and AUDIT-23 is the only audit whose roadmaps include AutomorphicPadicLFunctions; the string does not occur in data/library-coverage.json. The stage is real and carries text: title 'Hilbert Eisenstein theory and p-adic interpolation', status needs_source_decomposition, requires AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3, DirichletPadicLFunctions:KU-zeta, IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 and IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-iwasawamodules, consumed by IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-brumerstark and IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-oddmain. Its description says it is 'a readiness checkpoint ... an aggregation of those owners, not a new proof construction', which is why the severity is low, but it also says it 'Owns any missing modular-form and q-expansion prerequisites; no weight-two shortcut', which is mathematics an audit would have something to say about. Note that both the audit and REV-AUDIT-23 describe the scope as '45 batch layers' (the review's notes read 'Checked all 303 targets of the 45 batch layers' and 'Mechanically, all 45 batch layers are present'), so the stage may have been outside the batch the queue handed the auditor rather than dropped by them; either way the coverage record has the hole, and nothing in the audit says the stage was skipped or why.
findings.fix: Add one entry to research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-23.result.json under roadmaps['AutomorphicPadicLFunctions'].layers, keyed AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein, with verdict 'process'. That verdict exists for exactly this kind of stage and is already house practice: the integrated data/library-coverage.json carries 31 process entries, and AUDIT-01, AUDIT-03, AUDIT-06, AUDIT-08 and AUDIT-15 all use it, with targets and notes like any other entry (AUDIT-01's ComplexComparisonPartII:C6 is a worked example). The entry should record that the checkpoint aggregates AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 and IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 and constructs nothing of its own, so that its Hilbert Eisenstein and q-expansion content is audited at AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3, where the target 'Hilbert Eisenstein series, the integral q-expansion principle and the constant-term argument' is already marked partial with the F = Q pieces cited (ModularForm.eisensteinSeriesMF, EisensteinSeries.E_qExpansion_coeff, ModularForm.qExpansion_injective) and Hilbert modular forms recorded as absent. If instead the queue defined the batch as 45 layers and deliberately excluded this stage, the same entry should be added by whoever owns the batch definition, so that no stage of an audited roadmap is left with no coverage record.
